builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SimplexLoRA: Dynamic Rank Updating via Alternating Minimization with Simplex Projection
summary: SimplexLoRA replaces standard LoRA's fixed, uniform adapter rank with per-adapter importance weights learned on an n-scaled simplex during a short warm-up, then frozen, reallocating rank capacity across layers under a constant total parameter budget. The cost is an additional alternating-minimization warm-up phase and implementation complexity beyond standard LoRA, with no increase in inference cost or deployed parameter count. It can fail if the frozen importance weights, estimated early in training, misallocate capacity for a given task or dataset, since rank allocation is fixed after warm-up and gains are concentrated in low-rank regimes.
rationale: The method runs on a single GPU with no extra inference cost and code is available, but as a new variant its per-task rank-allocation benefit requires validation on the reader's own fine-tuning workloads before production adoption.
technique: Dynamic per-layer LoRA rank allocation via simplex projection

claims.statement: SimplexLoRA replaces standard LoRA's fixed, uniform adapter rank with per-adapter importance weights learned on an n-scaled simplex during a short warm-up, then frozen, reallocating rank capacity across layers under a constant total parameter budget. The cost is an additional alternating-minimization warm-up phase and implementation complexity beyond standard LoRA, with no increase in inference cost or deployed parameter count. It can fail if the frozen importance weights, estimated early in training, misallocate capacity for a given task or dataset, since rank allocation is fixed after warm-up and gains are concentrated in low-rank regimes.

Matches or outperforms standard LoRA and recent adaptive-rank baselines across 12 language understanding, summarization, and reasoning tasks on DeBERTaV3, BART-large, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen3-8B, with the largest gains at low ranks; no multiplicative factor is reported.
